newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS - Manila stocks seen wobbly ahead of GNP data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Manila stocks seen wobbly ahead of GNP data.

text.p: Philippine stocks finally broke their downtrend on Wednesday with the help of the U.S. Federal Reserve, but analysts say it is too early to say the worst is over.

"It was a knee-jerk reaction to a pleasant surprise. At least one of the negatives is out of the picture. But really, we are still in the bottoming process," said Raul Zamora, PCIBank Securities head of institutional sales.
The Federal Reserve announcement that it would not raise interest rates soothed jarred nerves on the Manila bourse where the main index closed nearly two percent higher.
The composite index gained 40 points at 2,538.97 after a 200-point loss in the previous four sessions.
"A one day rally does not make a reversal and volume was not that impressive," cautioned Wilfred Son Keng Po, chief operating officer at Angping & Associates Securities.
Analysts said the market was also boosted by the release of first quarter agricultural growth data of 4.22 percent compared to 2.49 percent in the same period last year.
The rise was taken as an indication of positive first quarter overall economic growth when the figure is released later this month.

"At least a portion of what makes up GNP is positive but we have to wait and see because the manufacturing sector seems to be a little bit disappointing," said Ramon Adviento, analyst at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
"Foreign players are still out of the market and I think they are just waiting to sell on rallies. If the GNP figure is positive, then they will buy up," Adviento added.
DBS Securities Phils Inc research head Francisco Trinidad said that unless the main index breaks through 2,600 resistance, it is unlikely that a reversal would happen.
Spillover buying may be seen on Thursday but analysts ruled out any sharp gains.

"The way trading has been going with market up two days and then the next day it gets killed, I would not be deluded that this is a return of happy times," said Gina Manzano, analyst at Philippine Asia Equity.

The Philippine equities market has been pummeled by worries that it was going to mirror Thailand's financial and property woes and lately by a possible U.S. interest rate hike and fears of an economic slowdown.
